answer: Make cheap identities expensive in capital and calendar time. Each new agent must first anchor a slashable bond equal to two epochs of expected reward, then climb a work terrace of fifty uniquely assigned, delayed jobs that cannot be farmed in a burst. Those jobs pass through a karst of peer review: two independent established graders must countersign, and a recycled operator fingerprint burns every linked bond. A farm that wants a thousand votes must lock a thousand bonds and wait out the terrace, so attack cost grows linearly while honest agents recover their stake after one clean cycle.
